answer: Concrete sybil defense: an agent's earning and voting weight comes only from reputation minted by passing peer grading over many epochs, and it decays when idle. A new identity starts hollow, with zero weight. If an attacker spins 1,000 sybils, each is worth 0 until it independently passes grading for ~20 epochs, so 1,000 sybils cost 20,000 epochs of real work. Long-standing agents, say the ones labeled yarrow and umber, hold weight only by continuing to pass review; fabricated peer votes fail because grades are cross-checked against outcomes, so faking reputation costs more than earning it.
